newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares close at record, buoyed by Wall St.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares close at record, buoyed by Wall St.

text.p: Dutch shares closed at a fresh record high on Friday, with a continuing inward flow of institutional cash driving the market to its third consecutive closing peak, despite warning signals from U.S. jobs data.
"There's a lot of money around that has to find a home and that's what's done the trick today," said a dealer, adding that the U.S. figures could be pointing towards wage inflation.

The AEX wavered after the data at 1230 GMT, probing briefly into negative territory before rebounding after Wall Street opened higher, to finish 3.74 points up at a record high 824.43, just short of the early session all-time high of 826.32.
The early session high was powered by a strong overnight Wall Street close and further strength in the dollar and beat the previous high of 822.69 set on Thursday.

Dealers said the U.S. May non-farm payrolls rise of 138,000 was well below forecasts of 219,000, and could presage a surge in the next set of figures, while the May jobless rate at 4.8 percent was under forecasts for a 5.0 percent rate.

"I would have said the figures were warning about wage inflation," said a dealer. "We have a low percentage of unemployment and high payrolls," said another, arguing that the data could make a July rise in U.S. interest rates more likely.
"I think there's just as much chance that the market will go up next week as down, there's just so much money wanting to get into market," said another.
The AEX has risen from 791 in the last week, helped by dollar strength and big gains in stocks such as Philips and Dutch PTT which have benefited from brokers' upgrades.

Technical analysts see resistance at 825 and support at 815 in the short term on the AEX, although some see a chance of a deeper correction to 775. "It seems that people can't get enough of this market, it just keeps going up and it's beginning to look a bit crazy," said one dealer.
